benchmarkContract: Coupled display:true window resizing, forced layouts, 1 ms scheduling wait, 15 ms inter-input spacing, 5,000 items, 100 durable burst/arrivals and functional invariants retained. Existing 50 ms input / 33 ms steady p95 thresholds now strict pass gates. Reports precede failures.
confirmed: The synchronous coupled NSWindow.setFrame(display:true) call dominates measured synthetic input completion. The entirety of RobotAppFrameView.layout is below 0.15 ms at every measured callback in stage A, ruling out its own geometry/backing-scale work as a material cause of47–52ms native resize.
limits: Synthetic offscreen own-process results are not physical input-to-display timings or a multi-hour memory/GPU stability claim.
notYetEstablished: Existing stages do not attribute work inside native resize/display to SwiftUI/native List layout, drawing or WindowServer calls. A2 adds public NSWindow.display/displayIfNeeded timings against the identical frozen production module; own-process stack sampling is requested.
productionChanges: Optional nil-by-default Robot frame-layout stage observer only. No layout/coupling/cache semantics changed.
status: Measured bottleneck located; optimization and repeated pass gates pending
